**upper_bound (I)**: Claim 1: For each prime p, gcd of the multiset of p-adic valuations is invariant. Proof: move replaces a, b with min(a,b) and |a−b|; since gcd(a,b) = gcd(min(a,b), |a−b|), the gcd of the whole multiset doesn't change.

Check: Is gcd(a,b) = gcd(min(a,b), |a−b|) valid for all a,b ≥ 0? If a,b both positive: gcd(a,b) = gcd(min, max−min) = gcd(min, |a−b|). Yes (Euclid). If a = 0, b > 0: gcd(0,b) = b; new pair: (0, b); gcd = b. OK. If a = b: new pair (a, 0); gcd(a,0) = a = gcd(a,a). OK. If both 0: (0,0) → (0,0). OK. Also gcd of multiset: replacing two elements a,b by min and |a−b| — does the gcd of the whole multiset stay the same? gcd(S ∪ {a,b}) = gcd(gcd(S), a, b) = gcd(gcd(S), gcd(a,b)) = gcd(gcd(S), min, |a−b|) = gcd(S ∪ {min, |a−b|}). Yes, since gcd(a,b) = gcd(min, |a−b|). The write-up states "Since gcd(a,b) = gcd(min(a,b), |a−b|), the gcd of the whole multiset does not change." This is a one-line but complete and correct argument; the identity gcd(a,b)=gcd(min,|a−b|) covers all cases including a=b and zeros (standard Euclidean identity, valid for nonnegative integers with gcd(0,0)=0). Edge cases: the rubric mentions "with the cases x = y and zero valuations handled" — the identity as stated handles them implicitly. Do we demand explicit case handling? The identity gcd(a,b) = gcd(min(a,b), |a−b|) is valid for all nonnegative a,b including x=y and zeros. I think this is fine — it's a complete argument since the identity is genuinely universal.
